box_status: Declared mathematical regimes, not measured nuisance bounds. The optical squared-amplitude box is a separate regime and does not contain the old t1=4/5 fixture.
decision_scope: Each listed scalar gap has a uniform lower bound >2/100 within its box, so the two point predictions expanded by epsilon cannot overlap at a common fixed parameter. Unknown independent parameters across rival models can still alias; no global inverse or empirical exclusion is claimed.
aliases_and_failure_regions: At eta->0, reset-CC and other count gaps vanish: no uniform separation over the whole charter.
At gamma=1, reset-CNC and no-click-is-ready continuation gaps vanish.
At r=1, no-click-is-ready continuation gap vanishes; no-click already leaves ready memory.
At eta*r=0 the click posterior is undefined; at eta*r=1 the no-click posterior is undefined.
Zero optical t1, a or r2 removes the dark-return continuation gap; zero environment coupling removes the norm defect.
One-bin p(C)=eta*r does not identify eta and r separately: (eta,r)=(1/4,1) and (1/2,1/2) share p(C)=1/4.
Local phase laws remain aliases on total N<=1; merged CP environments remain aliases on classical memory; sampled generators retain the clock-branch alias.
limitations: Readiness derivative bound is one-step only: no invariance or multi-step contraction of the readiness box is claimed
Only named scalar continuations are covered, not all frozen rivals
Common-parameter separation is not separation of full independently fitted nuisance prediction sets
Full programme identifiability node stays open under its prerequisite gates
